_about: Canonical source for IASC Reset indicators, reporting metadata, source-version notes and the reconciliation ledger. The extended Stocktake and assistant registry are generated from this file. Never change a value without recording the exact source version, denominator, reporting period and caveat.

stocktake-accessible-4page.title: Humanitarian Reset: Stock-take
stocktake-accessible-4page.version: Accessible four-page draft copy; filename includes 25 September 2026
stocktake-accessible-4page.note: Accessible copy reports 63% in severity 4–5 areas; 100M collective results including 40M with life-saving support; and 66M reached, including 41M in the most severe locations across 24 operations.

stocktake-summary-1page.title: Humanitarian Reset / Stock-take, October 2026
stocktake-summary-1page.note: Accessible one-page draft summary. Retains 100M/40M and 66M/41M framings and labels reach figures as not yet reconciled.

indicators.title: People targeted in the GHO 2026
indicators.definition: People targeted for assistance and protection in the Global Humanitarian Overview 2026.
indicators.caveat: A planning figure, not a count of people assisted.

indicators.title: People reached with some form of assistance and protection
indicators.definition: People reached with some form of assistance and protection.
indicators.caveat: Reach is not proof of quality, sufficiency or sustained outcome. Not the same measure as the 100M collective-results figure.
indicators.comparison_basis: 41M of the 66M were in the most severe locations (nested, not additional).
indicators.label: people reached of 148M targeted, by October 2026
indicators.note: Reach is not proof of quality or outcome.

indicators.title: People reached in locations with the most severe needs
indicators.denominator: 66M reached (63% as reported in accessible draft sources; 41M / 66M rounded figures yield approximately 62%)
indicators.definition: Subset of people reached who were in locations with the most severe needs.
indicators.caveat: The accessible four-page Stocktake draft and 17-slide presentation report 41M as 63% of those reached. Dividing rounded headline values (41M / 66M) gives approximately 62%; unrounded counts are not supplied. This is a source/calculation qualification, not a separate population. The 41M is nested within the 66M; do not add.
indicators.note: 41M in most severe locations; 63% as reported in accessible sources. Rounded 41M / 66M gives approximately 62%.

indicators.title: People with collective results
indicators.definition: The accessible October Stocktake introduction reports collective results for 100 million people, including 40 million with life-saving support. The counting method, denominator and overlap with the 66M Deliver reach measure are not set out.
indicators.caveat: Do not treat the 100M collective-results figure as the same measure as 66M reached. The accessible introduction says 40M had life-saving support; Deliver separately reports 41M in the most severe locations. The relationship and overlap of the 40M and 41M groups are not documented.
indicators.note: 100M collective results; introduction separately says 40M with life-saving support. Method and overlap with Deliver reach not stated.

indicators.title: People with life-saving support in the introductory collective-results framing
indicators.denominator: 100M collective-results framing (method and base not stated)
indicators.definition: The accessible October Stocktake introduction reports collective results for 100 million people, including 40 million with life-saving support.
indicators.caveat: This 40M figure is distinct from the 41M reported in Deliver as people reached in locations with the most severe needs. The sources do not establish whether the groups overlap.
indicators.comparison_basis: Do not add to or equate with the 66M reached or 41M severe-location subset.

indicators.title: People assisted who are in intersectoral severity 4–5 areas
indicators.definition: Share of people receiving assistance and protection who are in areas of intersectoral severity 4 and 5 (JIAF scale).
indicators.caveat: The website's cited 8 October revision records 62%, but that exact file was not available for this review. The accessible four-page October draft and 17-slide presentation both report 63%; neither provides unrounded underlying counts. The accessible documents reviewed do not support the previously listed 55% presentation value. Keep the version difference visible pending the exact 8 October file and calculation base.
indicators.comparison_basis: 2024 36%; 2025 43%; 2026 value requires exact-version reconciliation (62% in the site-cited 8 October record; 63% in accessible October source copies).
indicators.label: of people assisted are in severity 4–5 areas, 2026
indicators.note: Site-cited 8 Oct record: 62%; accessible October source copies: 63%. Exact 8 Oct file and unrounded counts required to reconcile.

indicators.title: 2026 HNRPs outlining steps towards responsible transition
indicators.definition: Humanitarian Needs and Response Plans with steps, milestones and timelines towards responsible transition.
indicators.caveat: The accessible four-page October draft says 75% (15 of 20) HNRPs in 2026, up from 40% in 2025 and 17% in 2024. The project implementation brief separately classifies the earlier 17% and 40% figures as cluster-plan measures. The underlying plan-level table is not supplied here; comparability of the three values must be verified before presenting them as a continuous trend.

indicators.title: Operations that have started or completed cluster simplification
indicators.definition: Operations that have started or completed simplification of cluster arrangements.
indicators.caveat: Started or completed, not 79% completed. No earlier figure is reported, so no trend is shown.
indicators.label: of operations have started or completed cluster simplification, Oct 2026
indicators.note: Started or completed, not completed. No trend reported.

indicators.title: Median days to complete the Humanitarian Programme Cycle
indicators.definition: Median planning time for the Humanitarian Programme Cycle.
indicators.caveat: Down 8 days since 2024; 11 days above the 160-day target set for end-2027. The target is not an achieved result.

indicators.title: Funding raised against the GHO 2026
indicators.definition: Funds raised against total GHO 2026 requirements, from 61 Member States and public and private sources.
indicators.caveat: The hyper-prioritized plan is 55% funded ($13.63bn of $24.94bn); the two denominators differ.

indicators.title: Country-based pooled funds
indicators.definition: Contributions to OCHA country-based pooled funds; $3.75bn of the 2026 total is US awards.
indicators.caveat: The site-cited 8 October revision reports $4.53bn as of 2 October; the accessible four-page draft and 17-slide presentation report nearly $4.49bn at end-September. The different cut-off dates may matter, but the records do not prove the cause of the difference. Contributions are not disbursements.
indicators.comparison_basis: 4.3 times the 2024 amount; no 2025 figure reported.
indicators.label: in country-based pooled funds, as of 2 Oct 2026 (×4.3 on 2024)
indicators.note: $4.53bn as of 2 Oct in site-cited 8 Oct record; nearly $4.49bn at end-September in accessible copies.

indicators.title: Cash and voucher assistance share of total funding
indicators.definition: Cash and voucher assistance as a share of total funding. The source material describes an envisaged target of 35%; it separately reports a 2026 CBPF allocation of $702M (32% of CBPF funding).
indicators.caveat: Do not confuse CVA as a share of total humanitarian funding with CVA as a share of CBPF allocations. The 35% and 85% targets are described as envisaged, not achieved results.

indicators.title: Local and national share of 2026 pooled-fund allocations
indicators.denominator: Excluding | including US Award Tranche I
indicators.definition: Share of CBPF allocations to local and national actors, direct and indirect. Excluding US Award Tranche I: 55% ($182M), 44% direct. Including it: 20% ($409M).
indicators.caveat: The site-cited 8 October revision reports 55% excluding and 20% including US Award Tranche I as of 28 September. The accessible four-page draft and presentation separately report 53% outside the initial US Award (40% direct + 13% indirect); the accessible presentation reports 55% for 2025. These values have different versions, bases and/or periods and are not a continuous trend. 2026 data remain subject to verification in H1 2027.
indicators.label: local and national share of 2026 pooled-fund allocations, 28 Sep
indicators.note: 55% / 20% in site-cited 8 Oct revision; accessible October source copies separately report 53% outside the initial US Award. Not like-for-like.

indicators.title: HCT seats held by local and national organizations
indicators.denominator: Humanitarian Country Team seats; seat count not stated
indicators.definition: Share of HCT seats held by local and national organizations, described in the one-page Stocktake summary as the primary authority indicator.
indicators.caveat: Representation is not the same as decision-making authority, influence or control over resources. The source does not provide the underlying count or a disaggregated country roster.
indicators.comparison_basis: No comparison series supplied in the accessible one-page summary.

indicators.title: Allocations to women-led and women's rights organizations
indicators.definition: Share of allocations to women-led and women's rights organizations against a 15% annual target.
indicators.caveat: Partial-year position; not comparable with full-year 2024 or 2025 results.

indicators.title: ERC–HC compacts
indicators.denominator: Number of ERC–HC compacts; count not stated
indicators.definition: Reported uptake of ERC–HC leadership accountability compacts.
indicators.caveat: A process/coverage measure of accountability arrangements; it does not establish the quality or effect of the compacts.

indicators.title: HNRP countries where HCTs regularly discuss feedback trends
indicators.definition: Humanitarian Country Teams that regularly discuss community feedback trends.
indicators.caveat: A decrease of 13 points. Not all Devolve indicators are improving.

indicators.title: Respondents who see coordination as more inclusive of local actors
indicators.definition: Perception Survey respondents perceiving coordination as more inclusive of local actors. 26% consider financial, operational and compliance risks equitably shared.
indicators.caveat: Perceptions of respondents; not representative of the wider humanitarian community. Delayed country responses may change the findings.

indicators.title: Respondents who consider financial, operational and compliance risks equitably shared
indicators.definition: Share of Perception Survey respondents who consider financial, operational and compliance risks equitably shared.
indicators.caveat: Perception Survey respondents are coordination actors, not a representative sample of all humanitarian actors or people affected by crises. Delayed country responses may change findings.
indicators.comparison_basis: Related but separate from the 56% perceiving more inclusive coordination.

milestones.what: Humanitarian Working Group endorsement of the Framework for the Responsible Use of AI in Humanitarian Action
milestones.evidence: Listed for endorsement in the Stocktake. No public record of endorsement located as of 19 November 2026.
milestones.qualification: Past due date. Do not present as endorsed until confirmed by the IASC secretariat.

milestones.qualification: Agreed actions and follow-up not yet verified against an IASC record. The EU statement welcomes an IASC commitment to convene regular meetings with donors.

milestones.evidence: Data collaboration is listed as an ongoing HWG workstream (presentation, slide 13).
milestones.qualification: Precise deliverable and owner not documented in the sources used.

milestones.evidence: Stocktake, Devolve: 2026 values are subject to verification in H1 2027.
milestones.qualification: 2026 local-share figures remain provisional until then.

milestones.evidence: Stocktake: mechanism piloted; to be institutionalized in 2027.
milestones.qualification: Pilot completed status and results not detailed.

milestones.what: HPC median planning time of 160 days
milestones.evidence: Stocktake, Define: 171 days in the 2026 cycle against a 160-day target.
milestones.qualification: A target, not an achievement. Current gap: 11 days.

workstreams.name: Simplified clusters
workstreams.note: Workstream reported complete; 79% of operations have started or completed simplification, so roll-out continues.

workstreams.name: Area-based coordination
workstreams.note: Workstream reported complete; 14 operations have sub-national area-based coordination.

workstreams.name: Complementarity

workstreams.name: Scaling the use of cash
workstreams.note: CVA 23% of funding (2025) against an envisaged 35%.

discrepancies.label: People assisted in severity 4–5 areas, 2026

values.value: 62% in the 8 October 2026 revision referenced by the website; exact file not available in the review archive
63% in the accessible four-page October Stocktake draft
63% in the accessible 17-slide October presentation

discrepancies.explanation: The site-cited 8 October revision records 62%, while the accessible four-page draft and 17-slide presentation both report 63%. Dividing rounded headline values 41M by 66M gives approximately 62%, but unrounded counts are not supplied. The accessible source copies reviewed do not support the previously listed 55% presentation value. The exact 8 October file and calculation base are required to resolve this.
discrepancies.do_not: Describe 62% as independently verified against the 8 October file, retain 55% as the presentation value without a supporting file, or substitute a derived percentage for the source-reported value.

discrepancies.label: 100M collective results, 40M life-saving support, 66M reached and 41M severe-location reach

values.value: Introduction: 100M collective results, including 40M with life-saving support
Deliver: 66M of 148M targeted reached; 41M of those in the most severe locations across 24 operations
Retains 100M / 40M and 66M / 41M framings; labels reach figures unreconciled
66M reached, including 41M in the most severe locations

discrepancies.explanation: These are not interchangeable measures. The accessible introduction describes 100M collective results including 40M with life-saving support. Deliver separately reports 66M reached out of 148M targeted, including 41M in the most severe locations. The sources do not specify the counting method or overlap for 100M, nor whether the 40M life-saving-support group overlaps with the 41M severe-location group.
discrepancies.do_not: Add the figures, equate 40M with 41M, or describe 100M as the same people-reached measure as 66M.

discrepancies.label: Country-based pooled funds, 2026

values.value: $4.53bn as of 2 October 2026 (8 October revision referenced by the site)
Nearly $4.49bn at end-September 2026
Nearly $4.49bn at end-September 2026

discrepancies.explanation: The reporting cut-off dates differ. The available records do not include the underlying contribution register needed to determine whether the difference is fully explained by timing. Contributions are not disbursements.
discrepancies.do_not: Describe the gap as verified growth, a correction or an accounting error without the underlying fund contribution records.

discrepancies.label: Local and national share of pooled-fund allocations

values.value: 55% excluding US Award Tranche I; 20% including it, as of 28 September 2026 (8 October revision referenced by the site)
53% outside the initial US Award, including 40% direct and 13% indirect
53% outside the initial US Award, including 40% direct and 13% indirect; 55% is the 2025 figure

discrepancies.explanation: The accessible draft and presentation report a 53% 2026 share outside the initial US Award, while the site-cited 8 October version records 55% excluding and 20% including US Award Tranche I. The presentation's 55% is separately a 2025 figure. Definitions, inclusion criteria and cut-offs must be reconciled against the exact 8 October file and underlying allocation data. 2026 values remain subject to verification in H1 2027.
discrepancies.do_not: Treat 55%, 20% and 53% as a single series, compare them as like-for-like trend values, or infer a change in authority from allocation shares alone.

discrepancies.label: Responsible transition planning, 2024–2026

values.value: 75% (15 of 20) 2026 HNRPs; draft text says up from 40% in 2025 and 17% in 2024
The site's implementation brief classifies the 17% and 40% earlier values as cluster-plan measures, separate from 2026 HNRPs

discrepancies.explanation: The accessible four-page draft's prose presents 17%, 40% and 75% as a transition-planning comparison. The implementation brief and current site notes classify the earlier 17% and 40% as cluster-plan measures. The plan-level source table is not available in the reviewed archive, so the measurement unit and comparability cannot be settled.
discrepancies.do_not: Draw one continuous trend or claim a 58-point improvement until the plan types and denominator for each year are confirmed.

discrepancies.label: Area-based coordination

values.value: 14 operations; seven country names are listed in the accessible four-page draft
Workstream reported as completed; not quantified on the slide

discrepancies.explanation: The accessible Stocktake gives a count of 14 operations but names seven in the list. The presentation reports the workstream as completed without quantifying it. Confirm whether the seven names are examples or the full list.
discrepancies.do_not: Infer that 14 is a complete country roster or that workstream completion means area-based coordination is operating everywhere.

discrepancies.label: Completed workstreams versus operation-level rollout

values.value: Simplified Clusters listed under workstreams completed
79% of operations had started or completed cluster simplification by October 2026

discrepancies.explanation: The presentation's 'completed' label refers to the workstream milestone; the Stocktake's 79% refers to operation-level rollout, combining operations that started or completed simplification. These statements describe different levels of completion.
discrepancies.do_not: Rewrite the 79% figure as '79% completed' or imply that every operation has completed simplification.

discrepancies.label: Defend evidence and measurement

values.value: Qualitative reporting; no numerical Defend indicator supplied

discrepancies.explanation: The accessible Stocktake describes advocacy, support for frontline leadership, protection, IHL/IHRL and PSEAH qualitatively. It does not supply a quantitative Defend score.
discrepancies.do_not: Invent a score, proxy KPI or numerical progress bar for Defend.
